payload.message: Review-artifact directory designation, run-wide. payload.question: Milestone m5 owns the one decision this vision explicitly reserves to the human: the public shape of raw= and on_issue= on fetch(), and whether RawMode stays a public enum. vision.md Open questions says raw= and on_issue= on fetch were not reached in the grill, and that whether RawMode stays an enum or becomes a boolean is undecided while being public surface. Measured at main 9725f16af881964903af9e556e96aa9e5c15a4ee: RawMode is a StrEnum with EXACTLY TWO members, OMIT=omit and INCLUDE=include, so a bool is expressible without loss of meaning; OnIssue is an internal Literal primitive; fetch is currently def fetch(selection, *, start, end) -> ObservationResult with NEITHER parameter, because milestone m4 deliberately deferred them here; ObservationResult carries raw: RawPayload as one of the four members #11 landed, and commit 7d0121b shipped opt-in raw receipts, so the capability is live rather than vestigial. The answer also fixes what milestone m9 must assert, because its acceptance criterion pins the exact public-name list and RawMode presence changes it from ten names to eleven. Escalated to the human rather than assumed: no ADR and no measurement decides public API taste, and nothing is published to PyPI yet so the choice is free now and not after issue #9.

payload.resolution: Human decided both parts. (1) raw is a plain bool on fetch: def fetch(selection, *, start, end, raw: bool = False, on_issue: OnIssue = "warn"). RawMode LEAVES the public surface and is no longer exported from rivretrieve.__init__; it may remain an internal implementation detail. The choice is justified by measurement: RawMode is a StrEnum with exactly two members OMIT and INCLUDE, so a bool expresses it without loss, and it spares the caller importing a user-facing enum, consistent with vision Scope-In item 1 that no user-facing object carries behaviour. raw=False keeps no receipts and raw=True populates result.raw.entries with the bytes parse actually read. (2) on_issue IS exposed on fetch with default "warn", so a strict caller can pass on_issue="raise" to refuse anything imperfect, while OnIssue stays an internal Literal and is NOT exported. Consequence for milestone m9: the final public surface is exactly TEN names, as_frame, fetch, fetch_by_provider, find, from_frame, map, pick, products, providers, to_utc, with RawMode absent alongside provider, observations, stations, provider_info, product_info, ProviderHandle and CatalogSource. m9 acceptance evidence must pin that ten-name set.

payload.finding: Suppressing stderr on a git push hides a failed push and silently breaks the PR that depends on it. Never suppress stderr on a push or a PR creation, and verify a created PR by reading the exit status or by querying gh pr list, not by pattern-matching the output text. Detected only because the human noticed no open PR existed.

payload.question:
m9-s1 has exhausted the falsification cap: 3 of 3 dispatches used, and dispatch 3 returned REVISE with one blocking issue, so the protocol requires escalation and a stop before any further executor dispatch, push or PR. A human decision is needed on whether to authorise one further bounded repair.

WHAT IS WRONG. Three instances of ONE defect class surfaced, each proven by mutation, each caused by the approved step plan rather than by executor deviation: a test was deleted because it CALLED a withdrawn public name, while the function it actually PROTECTED was ordered to survive. Instances 1 and 2 are repaired and verified. Instance 3 is _ProviderHandle.__getattr__, which plan section 8 explicitly orders retained ('Do not remove or change the internal _ProviderHandle; only the public ProviderHandle protocol is deleted'). It implements the provider-extras carve-out: forward provider-specific attributes such as cache_status() and refresh_cache() to the provider module, and otherwise raise AttributeError("Provider '<id>' has no attribute '<name>'"). At base 9725f16 exactly five tests executed it, all through rr.provider(<id>).<extra>: test_private_provider_handle_has_no_removed_declaration_methods, test_pl_imgw_handle_has_no_cache_controls[cache_status], test_pl_imgw_handle_has_no_cache_controls[refresh_cache], test_cache_carve_out_handle_contracts_are_explicit and test_ca_eccc_cache_lifecycle_remains_reachable. Plan section 4 deleted the first three and re-routed the other two off the handle onto the provider module directly. Only the CALL SITE rr.provider(...) was withdrawn; the SUBJECT survives. The same plan DID require exactly this kind of re-pin onto the surviving internal runtime for the observation and catalogue methods of the same class (test_public_observations_* -> test_registry_observations_*, test_provider_handle_info/catalogue_* -> test_registered_runtime_*); __getattr__ is the one method of _ProviderHandle omitted from that rename list. Consequence, demonstrated: the extras-forwarding contract and its AttributeError contract can be destroyed outright with the entire gate suite staying byte-identically green.

THE SWEEP IS COMPLETE, so this is the last instance rather than the next in a series. Round 3 measured whole-suite line coverage at all three heads, compared function-by-function keyed by qualified name, and validated the instrument by re-running it at b82d1d0 where it independently rediscovers the already-known _load_folium gap. At c6d27b7 it reports exactly ONE coverage regression out of 48 zero-coverage src functions; the other 47 were already uncovered at base and lost nothing in this step.

CURRENT ARTIFACT STATE, all verified at c6d27b73fc5efb04b692a068907888e02df1cc65: exactly one conventional commit above the milestone base with subject 'refactor!: retire the legacy catalogue surface' and no attribution footer; no tag; version 0.1.49 unchanged; empty diff over pyproject.toml, uv.lock, .pce/ and tests/typecheck/; no added noqa, type-ignore, skip or xfail; pr-body.md untracked; worktree tracked-clean; ruff, ruff format --check and ty all green; measured full suite exactly 1572 passed, 2 skipped with both importorskip guards unmodified. The vision's headline criterion already holds at this head: the eight withdrawn names are absent from dir(rivretrieve) and CatalogSource is gone.

THE REMEDY IS SMALL AND FULLY SPECIFIED by the gate: re-pin the __getattr__ assertions on the surviving internal runtime handle obtained from _registry.get(<id>) instead of the withdrawn rr.provider(<id>), keeping the forwarding assertions and the exact AttributeError message contract. It is test-only; no src change is required.

OPTIONS FOR THE HUMAN: (a) authorise one further bounded repair round beyond the cap, applying only this supplied required_change, followed by a verification dispatch; (b) merge m9 as it stands and record the uncovered __getattr__ contract as accepted debt with a follow-up; (c) return the step to a cold step-plan-writer, which is the protocol's ordinary routing for root_cause step_plan but re-runs the whole plan/execute/falsify cycle for the largest step in the vision.

payload.message:
Dispatch sequence 213, (m9-s1, falsification-critic) round 4 at ref 0f4c89a01badbe7c135a3a0f22c59d0fd9e59f19, produced NO verdict artifact and no result is inferred. It ran for roughly 26 minutes and then died: its entire captured output is one line, 'WARN pce: failed to deliver retained gate execution response error=Os { code: 32, kind: BrokenPipe, message: "Broken pipe" }' timestamped 2026-08-09T17:00:31Z, after which the log was never written again and no process for this repository remained alive. review-4.json does not exist; the falsification directory holds only review-1 through review-3 and their executions sidecars. The child transport broke, so this is an infrastructure failure and NOT a verdict: it is neither an approval nor a rejection of head 0f4c89a.

Diagnosis of why it was long-running and therefore exposed: the round-4 brief asked for whole-suite line coverage at two refs plus per-branch mutation runs, and a coverage-instrumented full suite is several times slower than the ~6.5 minute plain suite. Every other gate in this run completed in roughly 8 minutes; this one was an outlier by construction.

Remedy applied as an addition, not a replacement: reissue the verification with a tightened brief that drops the expensive whole-suite coverage re-sweep and keeps the mutation and shape checks. Dropping the re-sweep is sound rather than convenient: round 3 already enumerated the defect class exhaustively with an instrument it validated by rediscovering the known _load_folium gap, finding exactly one regression out of 48 zero-coverage src functions, and the only change since that measurement is the ADDITION of one test in tests/test_internal_registry.py. Adding a test cannot create a new coverage regression, so the class-closure claim does not depend on re-running the sweep; it depends only on confirming that the one added test actually covers both branches of _ProviderHandle.__getattr__. The step also still faces an independent pr-reviewer gate before merge.

Operational note for the remainder of this run: a gate dispatch whose brief requires coverage instrumentation or repeated full-suite runs risks this failure mode. Prefer briefs that pin a specific claim with targeted runs over briefs that re-measure the whole suite, and treat a dispatch that has written nothing for many minutes as dead rather than slow — the tell is a stalled log mtime with no live child process, not elapsed time alone.

CORRECTION of the immediately preceding delta at this node, which was FALSE and must not be relied on. That delta asserted that dispatch sequence 213, (m9-s1, falsification-critic) at ref 0f4c89a01badbe7c135a3a0f22c59d0fd9e59f19, produced no verdict artifact. IT DID. review-4.json (13,962 bytes) and its 198,550-byte executions sidecar were written at 20:14 local, roughly 74 minutes after issuance. The orchestrator misdiagnosed the dispatch as dead on three signals that were each individually consistent with death but jointly wrong: a single 'failed to deliver retained gate execution response ... BrokenPipe' WARNING line, a log mtime that had not advanced for 52 minutes, and a wrapper shell plus pce process sitting at 0.0 percent CPU. The BrokenPipe was NON-FATAL — it concerned delivery of a retained execution response, not the child's work — and the child continued running to completion. All three processes (69210, 69257, 90538) subsequently exited on their own; no process was killed and none needed to be. LESSON: a stalled log mtime plus 0.0 percent CPU is NOT sufficient evidence that a pce dispatch is dead, and a BrokenPipe warning about a retained response is not a fatal error. The only sufficient evidence is process exit WITHOUT the required artifact. Wait for the harness completion signal before concluding death.

CONSEQUENCE: two schema-valid verdicts now exist for the identical head 0f4c89a from two separate dispatches, and they DISAGREE. Sequence 213 -> review-4.json returned REVISE with one blocking issue. The later reissue -> review-5.json returned APPROVE with none. The disagreement is fully explained by orchestrator brief narrowing, not by critic inconsistency: after misjudging 213 as dead, the orchestrator reissued with a deliberately tightened brief that dropped the whole-suite coverage sweep and specified the carve-out check as 'break the AttributeError branch and confirm the test fails'. review-5 verified exactly that and correctly approved against its brief. review-4, working from the original broader brief, additionally checked whether the provider-specific AttributeError MESSAGE is still pinned and found it is not: the new test uses a bare assert not hasattr(...), which establishes only that SOME AttributeError is raised, while base 9725f16 pinned the text at tests/test_pl_imgw_module.py:78 with pytest.raises(AttributeError, match=rf"Provider 'pl_imgw' has no attribute '{method}'"). At head, grep -rn 'has no attribute' tests/ returns nothing, so replacing the entire message with an arbitrary string leaves the whole suite green at 1573 passed / 2 skipped. That is a demonstrated protection regression relative to the integration base.

RESOLUTION RULE APPLIED: the union of findings governs. An APPROVE produced by a brief that never examined a property cannot override a REVISE that demonstrated a regression in that property. m9-s1 is therefore NOT clean at 0f4c89a, and review-4's blocking issue is accepted. It is also squarely inside the human's standing authorisation, which required verifying that 'undeclared attributes still raise the provider-specific AttributeError' — provider-specificity is the message contract, which bare hasattr does not establish. The remedy is a three-line change inside the same new test, test-only, no source change, so no further authorisation is needed.

payload.finding: DELETION DEFECT CLASS, four confirmed instances in one step, each proven by mutation and each caused by the approved plan rather than executor deviation: A TEST DELETED BECAUSE IT CALLED A WITHDRAWN PUBLIC NAME MAY BE THE ONLY THING PINNING A FUNCTION THAT SURVIVES. When a deletion withdraws a public entry point, every test that merely reached the subject THROUGH that entry point becomes uncompilable and looks deletable, but the subject itself may be explicitly ordered retained. Instances found in m9-s1 of this vision, all in src/rivretrieve/_internal: (1) four tests for _filter_stations were deleted while _filter_stations, _normalize_string_filter and _validate_bbox survived as unreachable dead source with zero coverage once map_stations() withdrew their only caller; (2) test_map_stations_missing_backend_raises_fatal_contract was deleted while its subject _load_folium survived and remained PUBLICLY reachable through rr.map(selection) -> StationMap.render() -> _load_folium(), so the optional-dependency error contract of shipped code had no pin; (3) five tests pinning _ProviderHandle.__getattr__ were deleted or re-routed while the plan explicitly ordered that method retained, leaving both the extras-forwarding branch and the AttributeError carve-out unprotected; (4) the replacement for (3) used bare `assert not hasattr(...)`, which pins only that SOME AttributeError is raised, leaving the provider-specific MESSAGE with zero pins anywhere in the suite. In every case the whole gate suite stayed byte-identically green while the contract was destroyed by mutation. The plan was internally inconsistent rather than merely incomplete: it DID require re-pinning onto the surviving internal runtime for the observation and catalogue methods of the very same class (test_public_observations_* -> test_registry_observations_*, test_provider_handle_info/catalogue_* -> test_registered_runtime_*), and omitted only __getattr__ from that rename list. OPERATIONAL RULE for any future deletion work in this repository: for every test a deletion plan proposes to delete, ask separately whether its SUBJECT is being withdrawn or only its CALL SITE. If the subject survives, the plan must re-pin the assertions on a surviving call path and must say so per test, not authorise the deletions in one sweeping line. The cheap detector is a function-level coverage comparison between the integration base and the head, keyed by qualified name, with the instrument validated by confirming it rediscovers a known gap; that is what found instance (3) after inspection had missed it, reporting exactly one regression out of 48 zero-coverage src functions.
